page_title: A visual guide to SSH tunnels

summary.title: A visual guide to SSH tunnels
summary.one_liner: SSH local, remote, and dynamic port forwarding, ProxyJump, and autossh, shown with example commands and traffic-flow explanations.
takeaways: Local forwarding (-L) makes a remote service reachable on localhost; remote forwarding (-R) exposes a local service through the SSH server.
Dynamic forwarding (-D) opens a SOCKS proxy on the client that routes traffic through the SSH server.
Use -J or ProxyJump to reach a host through one or more jump hosts; ProxyCommand can route through a SOCKS5 proxy.
Enable GatewayPorts and TCP forwarding on the relevant side to expose ports beyond localhost; use autossh or ServerAlive settings to keep tunnels alive.
summary.summary: The page is a visual reference explaining SSH tunnels as encrypted TCP connections that carry traffic through an SSH server. It covers local (-L), remote (-R), and dynamic SOCKS (-D) port forwarding, each with example commands and a description of the resulting traffic path. It also covers useful flags, sshd and ssh_config settings such as GatewayPorts and AllowTcpForwarding, jump hosts, autossh for reconnecting tunnels, and an example for reaching a private git server through an intermediate host. The page is marked as a work in progress.
